# Legal-risk review set — machine-translated site content

**Generated by `scripts/i18n/legal-triage.mjs`. Do not hand-edit — re-run it.**

All ten shipped locales are machine-translated and carry `translationsReviewed: false`.
Reviewing all 1,982 keys in every language is not a task that finishes. This is the
subset where a mistranslation could cause a worker to miss a deadline, forgo a benefit,
or waive a right — and it is small enough to actually review.

| | keys | English words |
|---|---:|---:|
| full catalog | 1983 | 24,740 |
| **claimant-facing, load-bearing** | **150** | **5,181** |
| attorney-facing commerce (lower priority) | 1 | 8 |

## Review order
Ranked by New York workers' compensation claimant population, not by locale count:

1. **es** — Spanish. Largest claimant population by a wide margin.
2. **zh-Hans** — Chinese (Simplified).
3. **ru** — Russian.

`zh-Hant` is derived from `zh-Hans` by OpenCC and needs no separate review — fixing
a Simplified string fixes the Traditional one. `bn`, `ht`, `ko`, `fr`, `pl` follow later.
`ar` and `ur` are not built and not listed; they are on hold pending this review.

Reviewing this subset in the top three languages is ~15,543 words,
against ~74,220 for the full catalog.

## Categories

`deadline` time limit · `obligation` must-do · `filing` filing/notice requirement ·
`eligibility` condition on a benefit · `waiver` right that can be lost · `citation` statute or form

## calculators.aww  — 18 keys

- `calculators.aww.14-1-52-week-divisor`  *(citation)*
  > §14(1) — 52-Week Divisor: For workers employed substantially the whole year, total gross earnings in the 52 weeks preceding the accident are divided by 52. This is the default method for full-time, full-year workers.
- `calculators.aww.14-2-day-based-multiplier`  *(citation)*
  > §14(2) — Day-Based Multiplier: When the claimant did NOT work substantially the whole year, average annual earnings are computed by multiplying the average daily wage by a statutory multiplier based on the claimant's regular work schedule:
- `calculators.aww.14-multiplier-5-day-worker`  *(citation)*
  > §14 Multiplier (5-day worker): Average daily wage × 260 = average annual earnings, then ÷ 52 = AWW. Daily Wage = Total Earnings ÷ Days Worked. Then: Daily Wage × 260 ÷ 52 = AWW.
- `calculators.aww.14-subd-1`  *(citation)*
  > §14 SUBD. 1
- `calculators.aww.14-subd-2`  *(citation)*
  > §14 SUBD. 2
- `calculators.aww.14-subdivision-1-when-the`  *(citation)*
  > §14 Subdivision 1: When the claimant worked substantially the whole year, AWW = Total Earnings ÷ 52. This is the simplest method and applies to full-year, consistent employment.
- `calculators.aww.average-weekly-wage-aww-is`  *(citation)*
  > Average Weekly Wage (AWW) is the foundation of all New York workers' compensation benefits. Under Workers' Compensation Law §14, AWW determines the compensation rate — two-thirds (2/3) of AWW, capped at the statutory maximum set annually by DFS.
- `calculators.aww.calculate-average-weekly-wage-under`  *(citation)*
  > Calculate Average Weekly Wage under Workers' Compensation Law §14. Choose the applicable statutory method based on the claimant's work history.
- `calculators.aww.concurrent-employment-under-14-wages`  *(citation)*
  > Concurrent Employment: Under §14, wages from all concurrent employment at the time of injury are combined. If the claimant held two jobs, both sets of wages are included — even if only one employer's work caused the injury.
- `calculators.aww.disclaimer-this-calculator-is-provided`  *(eligibility, citation)*

- `calculators.aww.jsonld.free-nys-average-weekly-wage`  *(citation)*
  > Free NYS Average Weekly Wage (AWW) calculator under WCL §14. Statutory methods: 52-week divisor, 200/260/300 multiplier, straight divisor.
- `calculators.aww.jsonld.which-wcl-14-method-applies`  *(citation)*
  > Which WCL §14 method applies to me?
- `calculators.aww.jsonld.yes-aww-is-based-on`  *(citation)*
  > Yes — AWW is based on gross earnings including overtime. Wages from concurrent employment (a second job) may also be added under WCL §14(6) when the injury disables you from both jobs.
- `calculators.aww.jsonld.your-aww-is-your-gross`  *(citation)*

- `calculators.aww.straight-divisor-aww-total-earnings`  *(citation)*
  > Straight Divisor: AWW = Total Earnings ÷ Weeks Worked. Used by the Board when the §14 multiplier methods don't yield a fair result, or for irregular/seasonal workers, new hires, and part-year employment.

and the pages concern lead credits and refunds rather than a claimant's benefits.

## What was excluded, and why

A pattern match is a candidate, not a finding. These matched an include pattern and
were cut; run `--excluded` for the full list with examples.

- **25** — SEO metadata — search-result copy describing the page, making no claim a worker acts on
- **24** — navigation label or button — under six words, no rule stated
- **16** — product/feature description; names a legal artifact but states no rule, deadline or entitlement
- **9** — service-level promise about our own response time, not a legal time limit
- **4** — cross-link to another calculator; the legal content lives on the target page
- **2** — audience/marketing statement, no operative rule
- **1** — expired sign-in link — session UI, no legal content
